accounts: CRM does not store the login user or the tenant. `accounts.organizations` is the tenant: its `id` is `organization_id` on every CRM row, `business_type` decides B2B versus B2C versus B2B2C, and `industry_type` selects the field pack. `accounts.setup_users` is the person who logs in. `accounts.setup_user_product_access` plus `accounts.setup_roles` is how that user gets a CRM role such as sales_rep or finance. `accounts.auth_sessions` is the live login. `accounts.mail_oauth_connections` and `accounts.a2a_spoke_clients` are shared connection records. Reports join `owner_user_id` and `created_by_user_id` to `accounts.setup_users.id` so a metric can show the owner's name. They filter `organization_id` so one tenant never sees another tenant's rows.
cdp: CRM does not store the person's name, email, or phone on its own contact table. Those live in `cdp.customer_profile` and `cdp.identity_keys`. `crm.contact_profiles.account_contact_id` equals `cdp.customer_profile.cdp_id`. A contact report always joins those tables. Lead status, owner, company, BANT, and marketing opt-out stay on `crm.contact_profiles` because they are CRM facts, not shared identity facts. Soft-delete of a CRM contact is `crm.contact_profiles.crm_status`, not a delete of the CDP person. `cdp.products` is a different catalog and is not the product list CRM sells.
inventory:
The only product catalog is `inventory.products`. Quote lines, order lines, invoice lines, offers, add-ons, and price-book entries store `product_id` and join here for the product name, SKU, status, and billing type. CRM may insert and update existing product columns. It must not add columns. Revenue by product is the sum of commercial lines grouped by this id.

## Shared tables CRM uses outside Prisma
accounts.organizations:
Tenant root. One row is one Worktual customer organization.

CRM filters every query by organization id taken from the signed-in user. business_type gates modules. industry_type selects which extra fields a contact or company form shows.
accounts.setup_users:
Login user directory shared across Worktual products.

Deal owner, contact owner, and activity assignee store this id. A report joins it to print the rep name. Password columns are out of scope for both executors.
accounts.setup_roles:
Role name catalog. CRM maps the name into admin, sales_manager, sales_rep, presales, marketing, finance, or viewer.

The SQL executor uses the resolved CRM role to decide owner scope. It does not invent new role names.
accounts.setup_user_product_access:
Grants one user one role on one product. CRM reads rows where product_id is crm.

This is how a user becomes a sales rep or a finance user inside CRM. Reports do not change this table.
accounts.auth_sessions:
Live login session for a user. CRM uses it to know who is signed in and to revoke a session.

Session health is an operations question, not a sales KPI. The SQL executor may count active sessions only for an admin operations report and must not return token material.
accounts.mail_oauth_connections:
Shared OAuth connection for a mailbox. CRM also keeps product-specific connection state in crm.user_integration_connections.

A coverage report can say whether a rep has connected mail. The token itself is never a report column.
accounts.a2a_spoke_clients:
One Hub client id for this CRM spoke, plus the tokens Hub uses. Approved CRM-owned exception table inside accounts.

The reports agent does not need this table for KPIs. If an admin asks whether the spoke is registered, answer yes or no without secrets.
cdp.customer_profile:
Shared person profile. One row is one human the tenant knows.

Contact name and employer on a report come from here. CRM sales status does not. Join to crm.contact_profiles on cdp_id = account_contact_id and to crm.companies when the overlay has a company_id.
cdp.identity_keys:
Email and phone keys for a CDP person. Unique on organization_id, key_type, key_value.

Looking up a person by email or phone starts here, then joins customer_profile, then contact_profiles. A duplicate email in the same org is rejected by the unique key. Reports must not dump every email in the tenant unless the question asks for a contact list the role is allowed to see.
inventory.products: This is the shared product catalog in inventory.products. CRM does not own the table. A row is one sellable product with a name, price, status, and billing type. Quotes, orders, invoices, and offers point at product id so revenue can be split by what was sold.
crm.companies: This is the B2B account the sales team sells to. A row is one legal or operating company inside the tenant, with a name, optional parent for brand-to-store hierarchy, and a channel role that says whether it is a normal account, a franchise, an owned store, or a brand headquarters. CRM refers to this table whenever a deal, quote, order, invoice, contract, or contact must be tied to a company rather than only to a person.
crm.company_locations: This stores an office or site that belongs to one company, such as headquarters or a branch, including address lines and an optional region code. Contacts and commercial documents can point at a location so a report can split pipeline and revenue by site instead of only by the parent company name.
crm.contact_profiles: This is the CRM overlay on a CDP person. The person name, email, and phone live in cdp.customer_profile and cdp.identity_keys; this row stores the sales fields those shared tables must not hold, including owner, lead status, company link, BANT, nurture state, and marketing opt-out. Every contact report joins this table to CDP on account_contact_id = cdp_id and filters by organization_id.
crm.organization_profiles: This is optional CRM configuration for one tenant, keyed by the same organization id used in accounts.organizations. It holds the industry field-pack choice, internal email domains used to tell staff from customers, and related settings. Reports use it when a metric must respect tenant industry or internal-domain rules.
crm.deals: This is a B2B opportunity. A row is one sales pursuit with an amount, currency, stage, company, primary contact, and owner. Pipeline, win rate, forecast, and won or lost revenue are calculated from this table. Stage history is not stored here; the current stage and updated_at are the live values.
crm.deal_activities: This is the timeline of work logged against one deal: a call, meeting, email, SMS, note, or task. Reports that ask what happened on an opportunity, how many touches it had, or which tasks are still open read this table and join it to deals on deal_id.
crm.contact_activities: This is the same kind of timeline stored against a person rather than a deal. A call or meeting booked from the contact page lands here. Contact activity reports and last-touch metrics join this table to contact_profiles on account_contact_id.
crm.user_integration_connections: This stores one user's connected mailbox or calendar credentials for Gmail, Outlook, or Google Calendar. The reports agent should not read token columns. It may count whether a user has connected mail or calendar, and only inside the same organization.
crm.org_assignment_settings: This stores how the tenant wants new leads assigned, including the assignment mode and related rules. A routing or coverage report reads this to explain why an owner was chosen. It does not itself contain the lead rows.
crm.org_finance_settings: This stores tenant finance preferences such as default currency and invoice behaviour. Finance reports use it so totals are labelled in the tenant currency and draft-versus-send rules match the org, not a hardcoded default.
crm.payment_gateway_events: This stores a webhook event received from a payment provider after an invoice payment link is used. Collection and paid-invoice reports join it to invoices to show that money moved, including the provider reference. It is an event log, not the invoice itself.
crm.sales_user_assignment_profiles: This stores assignment attributes for one CRM user, such as skills or territories used by lead routing. Coverage and assignment-fairness reports join it to accounts.setup_users on user id so a metric can group leads by the rep profile rather than by the lead alone.
crm.product_offers: This is a CRM commercial wrapper around one catalog product, such as a named offer the sales team can put on a quote. It joins inventory.products so the catalog stays shared while CRM-only offer terms stay in crm. Reports that ask which offer is attached to revenue start here and follow the product id.
crm.price_books: This is a named price list for the tenant, for example standard or partner pricing. It has no amounts by itself. Quote lines resolve a price through price book entries, so a price-list report starts at this header and joins the entries.
crm.price_book_entries: This is one product's price inside one price book, including amount and currency. It joins price_books and inventory.products. A report that compares list price to the price actually quoted uses this row as the list price.
crm.product_addons: This is an optional extra that can be sold alongside a product. The row names the add-on and links it to a catalog product. Quote and invoice lines can include it so attach-rate reports can count how often the extra is sold with the base product.
crm.product_addon_tiers: This is a priced tier of an add-on, such as a seat band or usage band. It joins addons. A report that needs the add-on price uses the tier amount rather than inventing a price on the add-on header.
crm.proposal_templates: This is a reusable proposal document template for the tenant. It stores layout and default sections, not a customer-specific proposal. Template-usage reports count how many proposals were created from each template.
crm.proposals: This is a customer-specific proposal linked to a deal or company. It stores the document status and content used before or alongside a quote. Proposal pipeline reports join it to deals so a manager can see which opportunities have a proposal.
crm.quote_templates: This is a reusable quote layout for the tenant. It does not hold a customer price. Quote-template reports only count usage. The money sits on quotes and quote lines.
crm.quotes: This is a priced offer sent to a company. Status moves through draft, sent, accepted, declined, or expired. The B2B handoff to an order starts when a sent quote is accepted. Quote conversion and discount reports use this header plus its lines.
crm.quote_lines: This is one product, offer, or add-on row on a quote, with quantity, unit price, and line total. Product-mix and discount reports join quote_lines to quotes and to inventory.products. The quote header total should equal the sum of these lines.
crm.sales_orders: This is the confirmed order created from an accepted quote. It copies company, contact, deal, currency, and total, and receives a number such as SO-10042. Order reports join it to the quote it came from and to the invoice that finance drafts from it.
crm.order_lines: This is one line copied onto the sales order from the quote. Fulfilment and product-quantity reports use these lines. They join sales_orders and the catalog product.
crm.invoice_templates: This is a reusable invoice layout. It does not hold money owed. Invoice presentation reports may count which template was used. Amounts live on invoices and invoice lines.
crm.invoices: This is the finance document raised from an order. Status covers draft, pending approval, sent, and paid or void paths used by the finance flow. Revenue-collected and accounts-receivable reports use this table, joined to the company and the source order.
crm.invoice_lines: This is one billed line on an invoice. Product revenue and tax reports sum these lines and join them to invoices and inventory.products. Do not sum invoice headers and lines together or revenue will be double-counted.
crm.contracts: This is a subscription or term agreement with a company, including status, start, and end. Renewal and annual-recurring-revenue reports read contracts and their billing schedule. A contract is not a one-off quote.
crm.contract_billing_schedules: This is one dated billing event under a contract, such as a monthly charge. Recurring-revenue reports that need the next invoice date join this table to contracts. The contract header alone does not list each bill.
crm.audit_logs: This is an append-only record of who changed a CRM record and which action they took. Compliance and change-history questions read it. It is not a substitute for stage history on deals, because deal stage changes are not modelled as their own table.
crm.report_snapshots: This stores a saved result of a report so the same numbers can be shown again without re-querying. The SQL executor may write a snapshot only when the product asks to save a report. Live answers should still be calculated from the source tables.
crm.domain_enrichment_cache: This caches enrichment data looked up for a company domain so the same domain is not fetched again. It is a cache, not the company master. Company reports should prefer crm.companies and use this only to explain enrichment freshness.
crm.lead_enrichment_snapshots: This stores the enrichment payload captured for one lead at a point in time. Lead-quality reports can show whether a contact was enriched. The live person record remains in CDP plus contact_profiles.
crm.lead_enrichment_jobs: This is the queue row for an enrichment run on one lead, including status. Operations reports count failed or stuck enrichment jobs here. The business metric for the lead itself is not this job row.
crm.agent_step_events: This is one step an AI agent took, such as a tool call or a decision, stored for audit. Agent-operations reports count steps and failures. Customer pipeline numbers must not be calculated from this log.
crm.agent_input_fingerprints: This stores a fingerprint of an agent input so the same work is not run twice. It is an idempotency record. Reports use it only to explain duplicate suppression, not as a business fact about a deal.
crm.lead_summaries: This stores the latest AI summary text for a lead. A report that shows the written summary reads it. Counts of leads still come from contact_profiles, not from how many summary rows exist.
crm.notifications: This is an in-app notification for one user, such as quote accepted or a task due. Adoption reports can count unread notifications. It is not the business event itself; join the linked record if the question is about the quote or deal.
crm.meeting_analyses: This stores the AI read of one meeting, including summary and extracted points. Meeting-quality and coaching reports join it to the appointment or meeting session. It does not replace the calendar appointment.
crm.coaching_insights: This stores a coaching note produced for a sales user from meetings or activity. Manager coaching reports group these by user. They are observations, not changes to deal amount or stage.
crm.daily_briefings: This stores the daily briefing generated for one user. A report can show whether a briefing was produced. Pipeline totals inside the briefing text are not a second source of truth; recompute them from deals.
crm.privacy_requests: This stores a privacy request such as delete or export for a person. Compliance reports count open requests. Honouring the request is an operational workflow; the row is the record that it was asked.
crm.lead_nurture_jobs: This is the queue row for an automated nurture touch on a lead. Nurture operations reports count pending and sent jobs. Marketing opt-out on contact_profiles must be respected before any send is treated as successful.
crm.lead_lifecycle_jobs: This is the queue row for a lifecycle decision on a lead, such as qualify or disqualify. Lifecycle operations reports read job status here. The resulting lead_status is stored on contact_profiles.
crm.email_auto_reply_jobs: This is the queue row for an automatic email reply. Mail-automation reports count these jobs. The mailbox connection itself is user_integration_connections, and the person is still the CDP contact.
crm.gmail_push_watches: This stores the Gmail push-watch subscription for one mailbox so inbound mail can wake the CRM. It is integration state. A report may show whether the watch is active. It does not contain the email body.
crm.google_calendar_watches: This stores the Google Calendar watch subscription for one user. Calendar-sync health reports read it. Meetings themselves are in appointments and activities.
crm.calendar_meet_captures: This links a calendar event to a captured Meet session so the transcript and analysis can be tied back to the scheduled meeting. Meeting reports join it to appointments and meeting_assist_sessions.
crm.lead_scoring_jobs: This is the queue row for a lead-score calculation. Scoring operations reports count jobs by status. The score value the business sees is stored with the lead score result, not only as a job.
crm.meeting_assist_sessions: This is one live or completed Meet assist session for a meeting. Assist usage reports count sessions and whether a rep opened the panel. Transcript text is in meeting_transcript_chunks.
crm.meeting_transcript_chunks: This is one piece of transcript captured during a Meet assist session. It joins meeting_assist_sessions. Analytical questions about what was said belong to the knowledge-graph executor; the SQL executor only counts or fetches chunks the role is allowed to see.
crm.process_confirmations: This stores a user's confirmation of a proposed process step, so an agent does not apply a change the user rejected. Audit reports for agent actions join it to the related record. It is not a deal stage.
crm.agent_memories: This stores durable memory notes an agent saved for a tenant or record. It can explain what the agent remembered. KPI numbers must be calculated from deals, invoices, and contacts, not from memory text.
crm.a2a_spoke_tasks: This stores a task exchanged with another Worktual spoke through the A2A hub. Cross-product operations reports count these tasks by status. CRM business pipeline is still the deals table.
crm.appointments: This is a scheduled meeting or call on the CRM calendar, including start, end, guests, and links to a contact, company, or deal. Meeting-volume and upcoming-activity reports use this table. A completed meeting may also have an activity row.
crm.api_keys: This stores a hashed API key issued for the tenant. Security reports may count active keys and last use. The raw secret is not stored, and the reports agent must never return the hash.
crm.org_research_provider_configs: This stores which research or prospect provider the tenant has enabled, such as ZoomInfo, without putting secrets in the report output. Prospect-source reports use it only to name the provider. Pulled people live in prospect tables and then in CDP if imported.
crm.prospect_pull_jobs: This is one prospect-search job, including the filters the user asked for and the job status. Prospect operations reports count jobs. People already in contacts are skipped by the product rule and should not be counted again as new leads.
crm.prospect_pull_candidates: This is one person returned by a prospect job before or during import. It joins prospect_pull_jobs. A report of candidates versus imported leads joins this table to contact_profiles and must not treat a skipped known contact as a new lead.
crm.prospect_provider_cache: This caches a provider response so the same search is not billed twice. It is a cache. Lead counts must use imported contact_profiles, not cached provider rows.
crm.proposal_corpus_batches: This groups a batch of past proposals used to learn writing patterns. It is training content for the proposal agent. Revenue reports do not use it.
crm.proposal_corpus_items: This is one document inside a proposal corpus batch. It joins the batch. The knowledge-graph executor may cite it when explaining proposal language. The SQL executor only counts items.
crm.proposal_corpus_pairs: This stores a matched pair of corpus texts used to compare proposal language. It joins corpus items. It is an analysis artefact, not a customer quote.
crm.proposal_corpus_case_studies: This stores a case study extracted from the proposal corpus. Proposal content reports can list case studies. Won-revenue proof still comes from deals in closed_won, not from this text.
crm.proposal_content_playbooks: This stores reusable proposal content guidance learned from the corpus. It is read by the proposal agent. A report may list playbooks. It does not price a deal.
crm.proposal_corpus_jobs: This is the job that builds or refreshes a proposal corpus. Operations reports count job status. Customer-facing proposal status remains on the proposals table.
crm.proposal_playbooks: This is the active playbook the proposal agent follows for the tenant. It joins organization scope. Reports can show which playbook is active. Quote math stays on quotes.
crm.seo_projects: This is an SEO project record kept beside CRM for a tenant site or campaign. SEO reports count projects and join snapshots. It is not a sales deal and must not be added into pipeline.
crm.seo_tool_snapshots: This stores a point-in-time SEO tool result for a project. Trend reports order these by time and join seo_projects. Estimates are not Semrush results unless the Semrush source is actually configured.
crm.seo_generated_content: This stores content the SEO flow generated for a project. Content-output reports count rows by project. It is not an email sent to a lead.
crm.seo_keyword_queries: This stores a keyword query run for an SEO project, including the phrase asked. Keyword reports group these queries. Search volume is only a provider number when the snapshot says so.
crm.seo_saved_keywords: This is a keyword the user chose to keep for a project. Saved-keyword reports list these rows. They join seo_projects and are not CRM lead tags.
crm.seo_social_posts: This stores a social post draft or record created from the SEO flow. Social-output reports count posts by project and status. It does not mean the post was published on LinkedIn unless status says so.
